> Prime directive changed: **Joey gets a real, structured environment he can SEE and CONTROL.** No more agents editing opaque single-file HTML he can't steer. Keep the shader-union goal — lose nothing.

---

## 0. The ONE major change (in one line)

**Migrate Refract out of opaque single-file HTML into a structured Vite + React + React-Three-Fiber (R3F) Git repo where every shader is an individual, browsable, editable module in a Shader Registry — with per-commit Vercel preview URLs so Joey sees and controls every change.**

---

## 1. Honest assessment of the current state (why it is uncontrollable for Joey now)

On disk at `C:\Users\joeyw\Desktop\Refract\ANTIGRAVITY\MOBILE\`:

- **50 HTML files** of sprawl: `REFRACT_MASTER.html` + `v1`–`v17`, `REFRACT_APP_v35/36`, `CONFIGURATOR_v3`–`v34_AG` (30 of them), plus `App_v*.js`, `temp_*`, `audit_*`, `qc_*`, `server_*`.
- Each MASTER is a **single 30KB–250KB HTML file** with HTML + CSS + all GLSL + all app logic mashed together (`REFRACT_MASTER_v1.html` = 231KB). Nothing is a component. Nothing is diffable in a human way.
- **Three.js is loaded from CDN** inside `<script type="importmap">`; no dependency lockfile, no build, no types.
- **Every night an agent picks ONE file** ("the pretty v35") or **half-merges** (v17 wires the liquid raymarch face but gates it to the `Liquid` category only — `useLiquidFace(){ return state.category==='Liquid'; }` in `REFRACT_MASTER_v17.html`). Shaders from other versions silently drop.
- Joey's only "view" is opening a giant HTML file or a Vercel URL after the fact. He cannot browse the catalog, cannot toggle an individual shader, cannot review a change before it lands. **Control lives entirely with the agent. That is the problem he named.**

### Why this keeps losing shaders
There is no source of truth. "The build" = whichever file the agent opened that night. Deduplication has never happened, so each version reinvents or truncates the catalog.

---

## 2. Shader inventory — deduplicated by GLSL source identity (not filename)

Method: hashed every `FRAG`/`FRAG2`/`VERT`/`LIQ_*` template body, `SPECS` table, and `SHADERS` array across all 50 files.

**8 distinct fragment engine source bodies** (the real count — most versions just re-embed one of these):

1. **Named catalog gen-1** — `SHADERS[]` array, **80 named faces**, 3D-noise volume engine. Files: `REFRACT_MASTER.html`, `v1`–`v4` (hash `07029d5e6d`).
2. **Named catalog gen-2** — evolved 80-face `SHADERS[]` array. Files: `v5`–`v9` (hash `cf25fa1540`).
3. **Single field shader (object form)** — `SHADERS = {vertex, fragment}`. File: `v10` (hash `2d91dea049`).
4. **FIELD SHADER (DPR-aware)** — `FRAG`. Files: `v11`–`v12` (hash `76bdd2299e`).
5. **uMode multi-engine (early)** — `FRAG` with `uMode` switch. File: `v13` (hash `62418d79f4`).
6. **uMode multi-engine (14 branches)** — `FRAG`, `uMode==0..13` = 14 procedural faces (dots/metaball/lava/smoke/rings/matrix/strings/galaxy/gold/wire/iso/parallax/accretion/starfield). Files: `v14`–`v17` (hash `575564b254`).
7. **FRAG2 "v15 ENGINE" per-design** — 14 pattern algorithms (`pat()` mode 0–13) blended per design, driven by `SPECS` table of **62 named designs** across 14 categories (Field, Liquid, Lava, Vapor, Volume, Matrix, Strings, Signature, Gold, Gold Mesh, Density, Parallax, Eclipse, Diamond). Files: `v15`–`v17` (hash `1a5b1b4c1b`, `SPECS` hash `bb560cf63f`).
8. **Liquid raymarch OLED** — `LIQ_FRAG`, SDF sphere/metaball raymarcher (`smin`, `calcNormal`, 40-step march). Origin: `REFRACT_APP_v35.html`; ported into `v17` but **category-gated to `Liquid` only** (the exact half-merge bug).

Plus: **2 vertex shaders** (screen `VERT` + `LIQ_VERT`), the **62-entry `SPECS` design table**, the **80-entry legacy name catalog**, and **14 category→mode mappings** (`CAT_MODE`).

**30 CONFIGURATOR_v*_AG.html files** = watch-configurator UI/material/case shells (Tailwind CDN, no embedded GLSL engine). They contribute product-shell/material presets, **not** shader sources — keep them as UI reference, not registry entries.

### Registry target = union of everything, browsable individually
- 8 engine families → each becomes a module.
- 62 SPECS designs + 80 legacy named faces + 14 uMode faces + 14 FRAG2 algorithms + 1 liquid raymarch → each an addressable, toggleable **registry entry** with a live thumbnail.
- **Nothing category-gated.** Liquid raymarch is selectable for any watch, same as every other face.

## 3. Recommended platform (+ alternatives)

### RECOMMENDED: Vite + React + React-Three-Fiber repo (Git/GitHub + Vercel preview deploys), edited live in Cursor

Why this is the one:
- **Visibility Joey actually gets:** every shader is its own file (`src/shaders/<name>/fragment.glsl`) + a registry entry. He opens a Gallery route and sees ALL of them at once. Real diffs, real file tree.
- **Control Joey actually gets:** Git = every change is a reviewable commit; **Vercel builds a preview URL per commit/PR** so he approves before anything is "live"; `leva` control panel exposes every uniform (morph/flow/heat/palette/scale) as a slider he drives himself; dev server with HMR = edit a `.glsl`, see it instantly.
- **Preserves ALL shaders:** R3F's `shaderMaterial` helper (from `@react-three/drei`) wraps each GLSL pair + uniforms into a component; `vite-plugin-glsl` imports `.glsl` files as strings. This is the documented 2026 best practice for a componentized shader library. The 8 engines + all named faces port in verbatim (GLSL is unchanged; only the wrapper changes).
- **He is already here:** editable directly in Cursor, and he already has a Vercel `refract-app` target.

Concrete tradeoff: highest long-term control, moderate one-time migration cost (porting GLSL + building the registry). No shader is lost because GLSL bodies are copied byte-for-byte.

### Alternatives (evaluated, not recommended as the sole home)
- **Spline** (he has prior Spline work): excellent hands-on visual control of the **3D watch body/materials/lighting** and a Spline-style presentation feel. But Spline is not built to host 80+ arbitrary raw GLSL fragment engines — the shader catalog would be re-approximated or lost. **Best used as a complementary visual layer** for the watch shell, embedded into the R3F app, not as the shader home.
- **Framer / Webflow:** great visibility for the **app shell/marketing/onboarding** with visual control. Same limitation: raw GLSL engines only survive as an opaque embedded custom-code block, so per-shader control is lost. Good for the surrounding site, wrong for the engine.
- **Low-code / app builder:** gives control over app *flow*, not shader-grade rendering or a GLSL registry. Doesn't satisfy "control to design" at the shader level.

Verdict: **R3F repo as the core + optional Spline watch-body layer.** Web-shell tools (Framer/Webflow) are a later, separable decision.

## 4. Migration architecture for the recommended option

```
refract-app/
  index.html
  vite.config.ts            # vite-plugin-glsl, alias @shaders
  package.json              # pinned three, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei, leva
  src/
    main.tsx
    App.tsx                 # routes: Gallery | Configurator | 3D Watch
    registry/
      shaders.ts            # THE Shader Registry: id, name, category, engine, uniforms, defaults, thumb
    shaders/
      _lib/vert.glsl        # shared screen vertex
      field/{fragment.glsl,meta.ts}          # engines 1-4 field/volume
      umode/fragment.glsl                     # engine 6: 14-branch uMode (each branch = a registry face)
      spec/{fragment.glsl,specs.ts}           # engine 7: FRAG2 + 62-design SPECS table
      liquid/{vertex.glsl,fragment.glsl}      # engine 8: raymarch (NOT category-gated)
      legacy/catalog.ts                       # 80 legacy named faces (gen-1/gen-2)
    materials/ShaderFace.tsx  # drei shaderMaterial wrapper, one component drives any registry entry
    scenes/
      GalleryGrid.tsx       # browse EVERY shader as live thumbnails, toggle/favorite
      WatchScene.tsx        # 3D watch; face = any registry entry (2D + 3D share the registry)
      Controls.tsx          # leva panel: uniforms + palette + engine picker
    data/{designs.ts,palettes.ts,categories.ts}  # DESIGNS, PALETTES, CAT_MODE ported verbatim
```

Data flow (single source of truth):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  reg["registry/shaders.ts (union of all engines + faces)"] --> gallery["GalleryGrid (browse all)"]
  reg --> face["ShaderFace (drei shaderMaterial)"]
  face --> twoD["2D preview"]
  face --> threeD["3D watch face"]
  leva["leva controls"] --> face
  note["No category gate: any face on any watch"] --- reg
```

Key rules baked into the architecture:
- **One registry, consumed by BOTH the 2D preview and the 3D watch** — impossible to have a face that exists in one and not the other.
- **Every engine keeps its exact GLSL** — port bodies unchanged; only the material wrapper is new.
- **Liquid raymarch is a normal registry entry**, selectable everywhere. The `useLiquidFace()` category gate is deleted, not reproduced.
- **Gallery route = Joey's control surface**: see all N faces live, toggle any on/off, drive uniforms.

## 5. Migration steps, effort, risks, what NOT to do

### Steps (each is a small, reviewable PR with a Vercel preview)
1. Scaffold `refract-app` Vite+React+TS repo, pin deps (`three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei`, `leva`, `vite-plugin-glsl`), init Git + GitHub, connect Vercel preview deploys. Deliver an empty Canvas that builds.
2. Port shared `VERT` + define `registry/shaders.ts` schema + `ShaderFace.tsx` (drei `shaderMaterial`). Prove one engine (FRAG2/SPECS) renders.
3. Port engines verbatim into `src/shaders/*`: field/volume (1–4), uMode 14-branch (6), FRAG2+SPECS 62 designs (7), liquid raymarch (8), legacy 80-name catalog (1–2). Register every entry.
4. Build `GalleryGrid.tsx` — live thumbnail of EVERY registry entry; this is the visibility deliverable.
5. Build `WatchScene.tsx` (port watch geometry/materials from `REFRACT_APP_v35`/`v17`) consuming the SAME registry; remove the category gate.
6. Add `leva` controls + palette/category data (`DESIGNS`, `PALETTES`, `CAT_MODE` ported verbatim).
7. Reconcile against a checklist of all 8 engines + all named faces; confirm zero drops. (Optional) evaluate Spline watch-body embed.

### Effort
- Steps 1–2: small. Steps 3–4: the bulk (mechanical GLSL porting + registry entries). Steps 5–7: medium. No shader is rewritten, so risk is low and progress is visible per PR.

### Risks + mitigations
- **CDN importmap vs npm three:** pin one `three` version in `package.json`; verify `OrbitControls`/`RoundedBoxGeometry`/`EffectComposer`/`UnrealBloomPass` imports from `three/examples`. Mitigate in step 1.
- **GLSL precision/`discard` on mobile:** engines already use `precision highp float`; test on-device early via a Vercel preview on Joey's phone.
- **Bloom/EffectComposer parity** with the old 2D `UnrealBloomPass`: port pass settings verbatim (`0.95, 0.7, 0.0`).
- **Scope creep back into "one pretty file":** forbidden — see below.

### What NOT to do (hard rules)
- Do **NOT** pick a "winner" version again. The registry is the union; there is no chosen file.
- Do **NOT** half-merge or category-gate any face (no repeat of `useLiquidFace`).
- Do **NOT** make opaque agent-only edits. Every change = a commit + Vercel preview Joey can view before merge.
- Do **NOT** delete any existing HTML. The `MOBILE\` folder stays as the reference archive (additive-only doctrine).
- Do **NOT** rewrite GLSL bodies during migration — copy them; refactor only after parity is proven.
